fired.how: the point throws a failed fetch inside the try, as a dropped request's answer: the catch hands it to fetch_failed (a retry, or the fallback stands)
the point throws inside the try before the store call, a shared store's blip: the streak is said and the error thrown on
store_call throws on the point's failure: the guard answers its fallback (the page renders fresh and is not kept)
an outbox send's reply is lost after the receiver applied it: under_policy catches it and the policy tries again
the timing entry of a download never comes (WebKit gives a dropped one none): the wait for it runs out on this timer and the import reads as one with no response
a kept peer document reads as stale: it is served while one fresh flight refreshes it, and this handler keeps that refresh quiet when it fails (with a drop or down fault on the same run)
the point itself: a failed fetch thrown in the try, as a dropped request's answer
a lost answer that is not the last try waits its backoff on this timer, then fetches again (a retry the mutant cuts off: the hole never answers, the stuck oracle)
a navigation's page fetch the network drops (or cuts): it rejects
the failed page fetch answers no page: the navigation hands off to the browser (the mutant that keeps it leaves the tab stuck at the old page, the stuck oracle)
a hole whose server render throws answers a 500: the read refuses it, and the hole keeps its fallback
the refusal of that 500 (status N): fetch_failed retries, then the fallback stands
the point itself: a navigation batch's request fails before it goes out, as a dropped one's does
the batch's request fails (the point throws where net.fetch would): every hole it reserved is released in the finally and fetches on its own
the catch of that failed request returns: the finally releases every reservation, and each hole fetches on its own
the batch is answered 503 (the point swaps the answer, as a busy server would): nothing is read, and the finally releases every reservation
the point itself: a read of the batch's body fails, as a body that broke off does
the body broke off mid-batch: the catch returns, and the parts it still owed are released to fetch on their own
the batch's body goes quiet (the point reads as a stall past STALL_MS): the batch ends, and the parts it still owed are released to fetch on their own
the point itself: a step of the next page's build throws (its devalue did not load, a parse failed)
the staged build rejects: the navigation hands off to the browser, which loads the page whole
the point itself: the commit of a built page throws before it changes anything
a commit that throws is kept as out.failed: what was built is given back, and the navigation hands off to the browser (#276)

the point itself, on the 429's own throw: the answer comes back later, and fetch_failed waits (the Retry-After, else the backoff) and asks again, never gives up as on a refusal. The sim fires it at most twice in a document (CAPPED_POINTS), so a hole on its fallback at rest is a broken retry. Proved aimed (--buggify-aim hole.answer-later, gens 191 and 10: baselines clean; a 429 read as a refusal dies on gen191:1 by fallback-stands)

a batch part the batch did not carry is missed: its wait answers STALE, never an empty answer, so a joined binder asks again. Proved aimed (--buggify-aim batch.part-lost, gens 191 and 10: an empty answer in its place leaves the hole on its fallback, gen191:8 fallback-stands)

a binder that joined a missed part gets STALE and asks again: its own fetch runs. Proved aimed (--buggify-aim batch.part-lost, gens 191 and 10: one that returns the STALE leaves the hole waiting, gen191:9 stuck)
